tasks.short: Review a remediation proposal and tell the bidder the decision.

steps.what: Extract scope, method, price and exclusions from the remediation proposal.

loop.output: Rows for scope item, method, price and exclusion
loop.check: The manager checks each row against the proposal
loop.stop: One pass; a price with no scope item stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals mix a price table with narrative exclusions

steps.what: Compare the proposed method with the site constraints.
Flag a proposal that omits a permit, a waste route or a price.
Judge whether the remediation proposal is fit to award.
Send the award or rejection to the bidder.

loop.output: Bidder letter that states only the judgement
loop.check: The manager edits every reason before send
loop.stop: One draft; a reason that is not in the judgement is deleted
loop.why_not_simpler: The letter must follow the judgement, which is not a form letter

tasks.design: The proposal is extracted into scope, method, price and exclusions. Gaps a rule can see are flagged, and the manager judges the rest against the site constraints. The bidder letter goes out only after that judgement is edited.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proposals arrived as long documents, so price and exclusions were hunted twice.
tasks.enabler_now: A missing price or waste route can be flagged. Whether the method will work on this site cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Judging a method that is cheap because it leaves a constraint unmet.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which exclusion will reopen the contamination later.

ambition.what: A proposal is marked fit or unfit against the constraint list before anyone is told it won.

tasks.altitude: Review meetings stay. Hunting prices takes less time. The manager can hold a letter that praises a method the judgement rejected.

reach.task: Set the proposal tests that must pass before award
reach.learn: Which missing items are an automatic fail versus a question back

evidence.claim: A model can list scope, price and exclusions from a proposal; fitness for this site stays a judgement.
A policy library can map a proposal's obligations back to the rules it must meet.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. Boundary: from a received proposal to a bidder letter. Contract signature is a later negotiation.
Structured fields are scope item, method, price, exclusion and constraint id. The bidder produces the proposal; the site file produces constraints. Fallback: a blank price is a gap, not a zero.
Configure the gap rules before custom code.
Upkeep of 5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a new mandatory item on the gap list.
The letter is an external send. It waits for the judgement version.
unknowns: Whether bidders already use a common price template.
Whether award authority sits with the manager or a director.
research_questions: What share of proposals omit the waste route or a permit?
How often is the award judgement changed in the meeting?

incremental.description: Update the mandatory gap list when the permit adds an item

approvals.approved_version: bidder letter edited from the award judgement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: proposals are unstructured and the meeting reopens the method, so extraction saves little. High: prices are tabular and only the extract and the letter shrink. The award judgement stays.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the brownfield status report and present progress in the room.

steps.what: Pull brownfield status figures from the project record.
Draft the status report from those figures only.

loop.output: Report sentences that each cite a figure
loop.check: The manager deletes a sentence whose figure is not on the pack
loop.stop: One draft; an uncited sentence is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The report is prose, and a figure that does not tie has been a real failure mode

steps.what: Check every status figure against the project record.
Present brownfield progress and answer questions in the room.

tasks.design: Status figures are pulled from the {OPS_SYSTEM} into {BI}. A draft may use only those figures, and the manager checks them. The presentation uses the checked report and stays in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status was rebuilt from mail and diaries before every meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Logged decisions and quantities can fill a figure pack. Explaining a delay to the landowner cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Saying what a delay means when the figures are right but the room is not ready to hear it.
tasks.human_edge: The manager hears which number the room will challenge.

ambition.what: A status figure is either on the record or it is cut, before the meeting rather than during it.

tasks.altitude: Presentations stay. Rebuilding the pack shrinks. The manager can refuse a sentence that has no figure.

reach.task: Say which progress measures are reported outside the project
reach.learn: Which status figures may be repeated in an external update

evidence.claim: A compliance review partly drafted by a model cited sources that were not real, and the fee was repaid.
A status pack can be generated from logged project records; the presentation cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. Boundary: from the project record to a presentation of a checked report. The underlying cleanup is a separate task.
Structured fields are metric, period, value and source record. The project record produces them. Fallback: a figure with no source record is dropped, not estimated.
Configure the {BI} pack before custom code.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers a metric added to the pack.
External audiences see only the checked version. Unchecked draft text is not sent.
unknowns: Whether status metrics are already defined or invented per meeting.
Who attends the progress meeting besides the landowner.
research_questions: What share of figures already exist on the project record?
How often does the room ask for a number that was not logged?

incremental.description: Add or retire a status metric when the reporting need changes

approvals.approved_version: checked status report presented in the room

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the record is thin, so the pack is assembled by hand and the meeting is unchanged. High: figures are logged and only the draft shrinks. The presentation stays.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect the site, judge cleanup progress, and decide if work stops.

steps.what: Build the inspection points from the accepted plan.
Inspect the site and record damage and cleanup progress.
Measure what the inspection cannot see.
Compare cleanup progress with the inspection checklist.
Decide whether cleanup stops or continues.
File the inspection note and the decision.

tasks.design: The checklist comes from the accepted plan. The manager inspects the site, and measurements that need a laboratory stay with the laboratory. A stop or continue decision is filed only after the manager makes it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inspection points were a fresh list each visit, so progress was compared with memory.
tasks.enabler_now: A plan can generate the points to look at. Seeing the damage cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether what is on the ground is the damage that matters, or only mess.
tasks.human_edge: The manager sees the difference between disturbed soil and a new release.

ambition.what: Each inspection ends with an explicit stop or continue, not a note that is interpreted later.

tasks.altitude: Inspections stay the bulk of the week. The checklist is ready on arrival. The manager can stop work that the comparison does not support.

reach.task: Hold the next trade when cleanup progress is short
reach.learn: Which progress gaps must stop the following trade

evidence.claim: Site inspection of damage and cleanup progress stays with the person on the ground.
A checklist generated from an accepted plan is a rules task.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. Laboratory measurements are not the manager's saving. Boundary: from the accepted plan to an inspection record with a stop or continue decision.
Structured fields are inspection point, area, expected state and observed state. The accepted plan produces the points. Fallback: the manager adds a point the list missed, in the notes.
Configure the checklist on {WORKFLOW} before custom code.
Upkeep of 3 hours per 100 baseline hours covers checklist points when the plan changes.
A stop decision is an instruction to the contractor. It is not sent by a rule.
unknowns: Whether photos are already required on the inspection record.
How often a laboratory measurement is needed before the stop decision.
research_questions: What share of inspection points are visible without a laboratory?
How often does an inspection end in a stop?

incremental.description: Update checklist points when the accepted plan changes

approvals.approved_version: stop or continue decision on that inspection

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the plan has no coded points, so the list is written on site and the inspection is unchanged. High: the checklist is ready and only filing shrinks. The inspection and the stop decision stay. Laboratory time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep the record of redevelopment decisions, actions and progress current.

steps.what: Capture a redevelopment decision from the note or the mail.

loop.input: A meeting note or a mail about the project
loop.output: Rows for decision, date, owner and site area
loop.check: The manager corrects the decision text against the note
loop.stop: One pass; a decision with no date is not filed
loop.why_not_simpler: Decisions arrive as prose, not as a completed form

steps.what: Store the decision on the environmental project record.
Ask the author when the decision, date or owner is missing.
Close a progress action whose evidence is already on the file.
Hold a decision that conflicts with the permit or the cost.

tasks.design: A note is read into decision, date, owner and area, and the {OPS_SYSTEM} stores that row only after the manager has corrected it. Actions close when the evidence is already on the file. A decision that conflicts with the permit or the cost is held.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions sat in mail, so the record was rebuilt before each report.
tasks.enabler_now: A note with a date and an owner can be stored. A conflict with the permit cannot be closed by a rule.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing that a logged decision quietly contradicts the permit.
tasks.human_edge: The manager remembers which decision was a suggestion and which was a commitment.

ambition.what: A decision is filed the day it is made, or held the same day if it conflicts with the permit or the cost.

tasks.altitude: The week has fewer reconstruction sessions. The manager can hold a row that conflicts, instead of discovering it at the next report.

reach.task: Keep the permit version the record is checked against
reach.learn: Which permit version is current before a conflicting decision is closed

evidence.claim: A GRC platform keeps compliance, audit and incident records with dates and owners.
Logging a decision is a records task; judging a conflict with a permit is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the brownfield site manager. Boundary: from a note or a mail to a stored decision, a closed action, or a held conflict. Writing the status report is a separate task.
Structured fields are decision, date, owner, site area and evidence link. The note's author produces them. Fallback: a row with no date is not stored; the manager asks the author.
Configure the register on the {OPS_SYSTEM} before custom code.
Upkeep of 6 hours per 100 baseline hours covers decision types added to the register.
The stored row is the project record. It is not a notice to the regulator.
unknowns: Whether decisions are already written in a form or only in mail.
Who besides the manager may correct a stored row.
research_questions: What share of decisions arrive with a date and an owner already?
How often does a stored decision conflict with the permit?

already_counted.description: Chase a missing date or owner

incremental.description: Add decision types when the project record's list changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most decisions are vague mail, so each one is rewritten and conflicts are common. High: notes already name a date and an owner, and only exceptions are held. The conflict judgement stays.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still site walks, crew briefings and hearings. Constraint lists, permit fields and cost lines are ready before the visit. The manager can stop a method, a filing or a price that is not on a checked version.
reach: Construction managers: sequence demolition so contamination is not spread
Compliance managers: say which breaches are notified the same day
Regulatory affairs managers: keep the permit condition list current
skills_to_grow: Checking an extracted constraint against the source line
Reading a laboratory certificate without treating a blank as zero
Holding a filing or a price that is not the checked version
role.ambitious_version: Each site carries a versioned constraint list, each filing uses fields the manager has checked, and each on-site commitment stays inside a limit already signed.

job.title: Brownfield Redevelopment Specialists and Site Managers
